documents.title: Adult Care Facility Common Application – Schedule 6, Program Information (Part II) – Regional Office
documents.issuer: New York State Department of Health (Regional Office Part II review; Central Office project manager copied)
documents.how_used: This is the official Part II program-review checklist. It applies to new adult homes and enriched housing programs, changes of operator, and new ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP applications. The ALR and ALP applicant instructions say to submit only changed or new materials and to check 'No Change' where applicable. The 'required_items' list below uses the form's own item numbers. I left out paperwork that is not policy content: item 1 (application type check-boxes), item 2 (administrator/coordinator qualifications on DSS-3233, diplomas and transcripts), item 9 (Mental Health Agreement), item 12 (list of forms), item 15d–15f (support letters, nursing-facility transfer agreement, DSS contract), item 16 (waiver and equivalency list), item 18 (workers' compensation certificate), item 26(b)–(d) (dietary consultant agreement, resume and licenses), item 26(f) (kitchen and dining room diagram), and item 31 (resident fund account statement).

documents.title: Adult Care Facility and Assisted Living Common Application (landing page; applications are submitted via NYSECON, see DAL #19-16)
documents.issuer: NYS DOH Bureau of Licensure and Certification
documents.version: Current web page. It says applications must be submitted via NYSECON effective July 1, 2019.
documents.how_used: Context for how the submission is made. Schedules 1–5 are reviewed by Central Office for Part I approval. Schedule 6 is reviewed by the Regional Office for Part II approval. Part I and Part II may be reviewed at the same time, and final approval needs both. Model documents, such as the model residency agreements, are posted on this page.

required_items.text: Staff Orientation and Aide Training: Submit a copy of your proposed general staff orientation to be used for all employees.
Staff Orientation and Aide Training: Submit a copy of the initial training required for each job title that provides personal care, home health care and/or medication services.

Planned Staffing Schedule: Submit planned staffing schedule to be implemented upon approval of this application. Include: Adequate staffing for each shift on each day of the week; Persons trained in first aid (one of which must be scheduled for each shift); and The employee in charge for each shift when the administrator or program coordinator is absent; and All employees in all departments.

Resident Services: Describe philosophy, goals, and scope of your resident service program. (List cultural, spiritual, diversional, physical, political, social and intellectual activities to be provided by facility and community.)

Optional Resident Services: Applicant wishes to offer or continue a respite program; Applicant wishes to offer or continue a social day care program (see Schedule 7D); Applicant plans to use a portion of the requested adult home for purposes other than the operation of an adult care facility such as to house medical office for outside providers (submit a waiver request for section 487.11(l)(1)). For a change of operator application, the Schedule 7D applications for the social day care program must be submitted to continue the previous operator's respite or social day care programs.
Admission Policies (all applicants): admission and retention standards
Admission Policies (all applicants): resident profile that includes a description of any target populations
Admission Policies (all applicants): pre-admission evaluation policy
If you are applying for an Assisted Living Residence, also submit: ISP form, policy and process
If you are applying for an Assisted Living Residence, also submit: Palliative Care Policy (EALR and SNALR)
Resident Fund Accounts. NOTE: You must offer resident fund accounts for residents who are SSI and/or SNA recipients, even if you do not accept SSI/SNA as payment in full.
Disaster and Emergency Plan: Submit a copy of your disaster and emergency plan, including evacuation procedures.

Medication Management Policies and Procedures. NOTE: Applicant must apply for a Class 3A limited controlled substance license. This is typically done just prior to the regional office's on-site inspection.

EALR Policies and Procedures: For EALR only, submit copies of all policies and procedures for skilled nursing services and those HHA services above and beyond what resident care aides may deliver, to be delivered directly by Operator's staff. This list of policies must match the list of services in your EALR addendum. Any addition or deletion of EALR services must be prior approved by the regional office.
SNALR Policies and Procedures: For SNALRs only, submit a copy of your: dementia unit/SNALR plan
SNALR Policies and Procedures: For SNALRs only, submit a copy of your: dementia unit/SNALR activities schedule
ALP Program Information (newly established ALPs): Describe the anticipated sources of referral to, and discharge from, the ALP and describe the proposed relationship with these sources.
ALP Program Information: Will the ALP be located in the same building with non-ALP adult home or enriched housing beds? If yes, describe how the ALP will relate to these services programmatically.
ALP Program Information: Describe the proposed site for the ALP including physical relationship with and access to community services.
Personnel Policies and Procedures: Include the following: rules of conduct, facility policy regarding grievance procedures, hiring and termination policies.
Job Descriptions for all staff positions: For EALRs and ALPS that employ Home Health Aides (HHAs), include the tasks that HHAs are authorized to perform, which must be within the HHA scope of tasks.
In-Service Training, 12 month in-service schedule
Activity Schedule for One Month
Social Contact: A description of how the facility will encourage contact between residents, relatives and friends.
House Rules, if any
Resident Organizations and, if SNALR, Family Organization Policies
A Description of Special Services, if any

Food Services, including: three weeks of menus for meals and snacks, including the special modified diets offered including diets such as finger foods and consistency modifications, and a definition of each diet offered. Include the times of each meal and snack service
Food Services, including: policy and procedure for kitchen staff to have current and accurate information regarding each resident's prescribed diet, allergies, food preferences and any changes.
Food Services, including: policy and procedure for food purchase and storage.
Food Services, including: policy and procedure to ensure meals and snacks are handled properly to ensure proper temperatures and other food protections.
Food Services, including: policy on food service staff training.
Volunteer Policy and Orientation, if volunteers are to be used in the facility
Record Keeping policy for maintaining records and reports
Housekeeping Plan
Maintenance Plan

Any entity applying to operate an ACF or certify additional beds in an ACF must develop and submit admission procedures and policies, including a non-discrimination statement and reasonable accommodation policy, consistent with ACF DAL# DACF 23-15.

notes: The reviewer is the DOH Regional Office for the county where the facility is or will be. Each of the 32 items on DOH-5098 is a numbered section, and the manual should follow that numbering. For each item, the applicant gives an attachment number or checks 'No Change' (on items that have that box). The ALR and ALP instructions limit responses to changed or new materials. Items 13 (EALR), 14 (SNALR) and 15 (ALP) apply only to those license types. Item 15 is completed in full (15a–15f) for a newly established ALP. For a change of operator, only 15e–15f are completed. The completed Schedule 6 is submitted with a cover letter to the regional office, with a copy of the cover letter to the assigned Central Office project manager in Albany. It can be submitted at any time, but no later than 90 days after the Part I approval notice. Applications go in through NYSECON. Any substitute for a DOH-mandated form must be listed under item 12 and needs an equivalency (see item 16). Model documents, such as the model residency agreements, are posted on the Common Application web page. Items 17, 20 and 26 spell out their own sub-requirements, so keep that wording inside those sections. The regulations cited in the request (18 NYCRR Parts 487, 488 and 494; 10 NYCRR Part 1001) set the substantive standards behind these items. Schedule 6 is the single official checklist used for the review, so I did not pull items from those regulations.
